result.topic_en: Euler substitutes fractions for the letters in Theorem VI to obtain Theorem VII, which converts an alternating series into a continued fraction; he applies it to the series summing to (√2−1)/√2 to get a continued fraction for √2, and then states Problem IV on converting a power series in x into a continued fraction.
result.transcription:
) 164 (
§. 43. Quodsi in serie Theorematis VI loco litterarum $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. scribantur fractiones
$\frac{\alpha}{a}, \frac{\beta}{b}, \frac{\gamma}{c}, \frac{\delta}{d}$ etc., vt sit
$s = \frac{a}{\alpha} - \frac{ab}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{abc}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{abcd}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
fractio continua hinc nata erit
$\frac{1}{s} = \frac{\alpha}{a} + \cfrac{\alpha:a}{\frac{\beta}{b} - 1 + \cfrac{\beta:b}{\frac{\gamma}{c} - 1 + \cfrac{\gamma:c}{\frac{\delta}{d} - 1 + \text{etc.}}}}$
Quodsi iam primo multiplicetur vtrinque per $a$, tum vero prima fractio supra et infra per $b$, secunda per $c$, tertia per $d$, etc., orietur ista forma:
$\frac{a}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha b}{\beta - b + \cfrac{\beta c}{\gamma - c + \cfrac{\gamma d}{\delta - d + \text{etc.}}}}$
quod sequenti Theoremati includatur
Theorema VII.
§. 44. Si proposita fuerit huiusmodi series infinita:
$s = \frac{a}{\alpha} - \frac{ab}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{abc}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{abcd}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
inde deducitur haec fractio continua:
$\frac{a}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha b}{\beta - b + \cfrac{\beta c}{\gamma - c + \cfrac{\gamma d}{\delta - d + \text{etc.}}}}$
§. 45.

) 165 (
§. 45. Applicemus hoc ad sequentem seriem infinitam:
$s = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1.3}{2.4} + \frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6} - \frac{1.3.5.7}{2.4.6.8} + \text{etc.}$
cuius summam constat esse $s = \frac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{\sqrt{2}}$; tum igitur erit
$a = 1, b = 3, c = 5, d = 7$, etc.
$\alpha = 2, \beta = 4, \gamma = 6, \delta = 8$, etc.
fractio ergo continua hinc nata erit
$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = 2 + \cfrac{2.3}{1 + \cfrac{4.5}{1 + \cfrac{6.7}{1 + \text{etc.}}}}$
Si vtrinque vnitas auferatur erit
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = 1 + \cfrac{2.3}{1 + \cfrac{4.5}{1 + \cfrac{6.7}{1 + \text{etc.}}}}$
vnde deducitur
$\sqrt{2} = 1 + \cfrac{1.1}{1 + \cfrac{2.3}{1 + \cfrac{4.5}{1 + \cfrac{6.7}{1 + \text{etc.}}}}}$
Problema IV.
Propositam seriem infinitam huius formae:
$s = \frac{x}{\alpha} - \frac{xx}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{x^3}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{x^4}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
in fractionem continuam conuertere.
X 3 Solutio

items.quote:
Si proposita fuerit huiusmodi series infinita:
$s = \frac{a}{\alpha} - \frac{ab}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{abc}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{abcd}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
inde deducitur haec fractio continua:
items.english: Theorem VII: If an infinite series of the form s = a/α − ab/αβ + abc/αβγ − abcd/αβγδ + etc. is proposed, the continued fraction a/s = α + αb/(β − b + βc/(γ − c + γd/(δ − d + etc.))) follows from it.
The sum of the series 1/2 − 1·3/2·4 + 1·3·5/2·4·6 − … is known to be (√2 − 1)/√2.
